clue.text: Hazard on course from which European's sliced clear

parts.note: on a golf course the rough is a hazard, giving the rough

explanation.surface: A golfer's ball slices out of the long grass and away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sliced' plays on the golf shot, but here it means the E of THE ROUGH is cut out.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, clear can mean all the way, as in going right from one side to the other.

clue.text: Transporting Tito to Blenheim, one's lost balance here

indicators.note: transporting means carrying away, so the letters are moved around
lost means one letter is missing from the rearranged set

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Carrying a Yugoslav leader to a palace, someone tips over.
explanation.walkthrough: TITOTOBLENHEIM less one I is rearranged; Blenheim Palace is a stately home in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The final figure in an account showing profit or loss is the balance.

clue.text: Double agent's picked up alcoholic drinks

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the alcohol word is taken by its sound

parts.note: liquor is spirits, alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A spy who works for both sides has spotted strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, liquor sounds like the ending of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact copy is a double of the original.

clue.text: Take tackle out, rolling around in rug

explanation.surface: Someone strips the rigging off a boat while tumbling on a carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle on a ship is its rigging, so removing it means stripping a vessel.

clue.text: Two taps on a piano conceal one disadvantage

parts.note: taps are marked H and C, hot and cold, giving H and C

explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is something that hinders progress, a drawback.

clue.text: 16 books in package

indicators.note: in puts the pair of letters for books inside the word for a package

parts.note: a bale is a large bound package, as of hay or cotton

explanation.surface: Sixteen books arrive in a single parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: '16' refers to the answer of 16 Down, baby talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless prattle like an infant's is what baby talk sounds like: a synonym.

clue.text: Is employed by Times, concealing medical procedure — this one?

definitions.note: this one refers back to medical procedure, so it is a procedure

indicators.note: employed by means taken on inside, so IS sits within the multiplication word

parts.note: by means times, as in three by four

indicators.note: concealing means hiding within, so the procedure goes inside IS

parts.note: an op is an operation

explanation.surface: Something is used by a newspaper to hide a hospital operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This one?' points back to 'medical procedure': the answer is one such procedure. Times is set in italics, as if the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking tissue to examine for disease is a diagnostic medical procedure.

clue.text: Topic of one poem by Milton, and one executed in ignorance?

definitions.text: Topic of one poem by Milton

indicators.note: in places the two beheaded words inside the word for ignorance

parts.note: ignorance is bliss, as the proverb says

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so each of the two words loses its head letter

explanation.surface: Milton wrote of a subject, and of someone put to death without knowing why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' strips the first letters of AND and ONE to leave ND and NE; Milton's sonnet 'On His Blindness' supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton went sightless in middle age and wrote a famous sonnet about losing his sight.

clue.text: Serious condition not at first a bar to conversation

indicators.note: not at first means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a block is a bar, an obstruction
jaw is slang for talk, chatter

explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is commonly called this, after its spasms of the jaw muscles.

clue.text: Was enough for augmenting particularly English language

parts.note: esp. is the standard abbreviation for especially, i.e. particularly

explanation.surface: Something proved sufficient to boost a particular English tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the best known artificial international tongue, devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

explanation.definitionFit: The topic being dealt with is the material at hand.

clue.text: Lowly team's record, grand in red?

parts.note: a lowly team's record of results might be nought, one win: O for nought plus WIN
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A poor side's results include a thousand pounds sunk in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the red means having debts outstanding to someone.

clue.text: In turn, European country shortly admitting bogus religion as breach of trust

clue.text: Impetuous rip-off?

definitions.meaning: a reckless, wild young person, used here as an adjective
to rip off something is to pull or tear it away

explanation.definitionFit: A reckless hooligan is called this; tearing something away is ripping it off.

clue.text: A letter on its own, in a funny sort of way

definitions.text: in a funny sort of way

parts.note: mu is a Greek letter
singly means one at a time, alone

explanation.surface: A single letter by itself seems comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a way that causes laughter is doing it comically.

clue.text: "Green veg", one's told by little bird in Scotland

parts.note: a pea is a green vegetable
wee means little, especially in Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the lapwing is called this, from its cry.

clue.text: Sick tabby starts to act like kitten —- going ga-ga?

starts to picks the first letter of each following word

clue.text: Mark, pursuing mother antelope, shows bottle

clue.text: Anatomist holding volume —— it shows seriousness

parts.note: Henry Gray wrote Gray's Anatomy, the medical textbook

clue.text: Composer's triteness amazing? Not entirely, in retrospect

not entirely means only part of the phrase is used, a run of its letters

clue.text: Might it be Sky Two initially received, being in range when hooked up?

taken as written

clue.text: Enthusiastically crossing the M1?

clue.text: Possible cover for those who serve Cape — excessive area

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
